title: Joint Advisory: Ransomware Targeting Healthcare and Public Health Sector Entities
summary: A joint federal advisory describes ransomware operators repeatedly targeting hospital systems, exfiltrating patient records before encryption and timing deployment to coincide with reduced staffing.
content:
## Summary

The authoring agencies are releasing this advisory to inform health sector defenders of observed activity. A joint federal advisory describes ransomware operators repeatedly targeting hospital systems, exfiltrating patient records before encryption and timing deployment to coincide with reduced staffing.

**Advisory type:** Joint Cybersecurity Advisory

**Authoring agencies:** CISA, FBI, HHS

## Observed tactics, techniques and procedures

- Initial access through exposed remote access services and unpatched public-facing applications
- Credential theft followed by lateral movement into imaging and records infrastructure
- Bulk exfiltration to commercial cloud storage before any encryption occurs
- Deletion of volume shadow copies and stopping of backup services immediately prior to encryption

## Recommended actions

- Maintain offline, tested backups of clinical systems and verify restoration end to end.
- Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication on all remote access.
- Segment clinical networks so that records, imaging and biomedical devices do not share a broadcast domain.
- Rehearse extended downtime procedures with clinical staff, not only with IT staff.

## Defender considerations

- Exfiltration now precedes encryption in most observed intrusions, so an organisation that restores cleanly from backup still faces a disclosure event.
- Deployment is repeatedly timed to weekends and holiday periods when clinical and IT staffing is lowest.
- The operational impact begins with diversion of emergency admissions, which is a clinical outcome before it is a technical one.
